topic: LLM agents and agentic systems that develop machine-learning models: agentic AutoML, LLM-driven hyperparameter and architecture search, LLM agents that diagnose why a trained model fails and choose a remedy, and comparisons of such agents against plain optimizers (Bayesian optimization, Optuna). Prioritize any use of agents to build or tune graph neural networks or other surrogates for lattice / architected materials, then materials science and mechanics more broadly. Report honestly if none exist for lattice GNNs specifically.
name: agents
final_message:
I couldn't write the review. My first `write_review` call was denied: Bash permission was refused because Claude Code is in don't-ask mode. I haven't tried another way to write it, so no review file exists yet. The 34 `record_paper` entries went through earlier and should still be saved under the `agents` folder.

**What I need from you:** allow the `python -m agents.literature.cli write_review --name agents ...` command, or tell me to write it another way. I'll then write the review in the planned parts (overview, dataset, other datasets, models table, baselines, symmetry, labels, defects, gaps, references). I have the text drafted.

**What the recorded papers show:**
- **Lattice GNNs:** I found no paper where an LLM agent builds or tunes a GNN for lattice or architected-material stiffness. The metamaterial hits were agents that design structures, photonic work, or reviews. That is limited to my arXiv and OpenAlex searches.
- **Agent against Optuna and BO:** the evidence conflicts, and the setup explains why.
  - With a fixed search space and a long budget, CMA-ES, TPE and SMAC beat LLM agents. The best result was a hybrid where the LLM acts on only 30% of trials [Ferreira 2026, p. 5, p. 7-8].
  - With about 5 sequential runs where the agent reads logs, strong agents beat TPE and random search in aggregate [Huai 2026, p. 8]. Only 2 of its 30 tasks are graph tasks.
  - When the agent can call an optimizer as a tool, it beat the best numerical optimizer in 4 of 5 domains [Chen 2026, abstract; I did not read its result tables].
- **Failure diagnosis:** agents diagnose model failures only as standalone tools (MLIP Detective, abstract only) or as accept/reject gates inside a tuning loop [Osaro 2026, p. 3]. I found no end-to-end diagnose-then-fix agent for a materials surrogate.

**The 3 most relevant papers:**
1. **Zhang & Yakobson 2026** (2606.29717): a coding agent built the best from-scratch crystal graph network on MatBench band gap (0.1480 eV). It also ran on a log10 shear-modulus task. Its accepted changes were all known methods, the model did not transfer to other tasks, and a residual-correlation "crowding score" got it unstuck [p. 1, 5, 6].
2. **Ferreira et al. 2026** (2603.24647): the most direct agent-versus-optimizer comparison, and the source of the hybrid design above.
3. **Osaro et al. 2026** (MLIPilot, 2605.30889): an agent edits a MACE model and is only allowed to keep changes that pass hard physical gates. For us the analogue would be a positive-definite stiffness matrix and bounded Poisson ratios.

**Gaps I could not fill:**
- I did not verify the Lumpe & Stankovic dataset (relative density, how C and n were fitted, strut model, the 41 excluded lattices) because this run was about agents.
- I did not look for baselines on our dataset through citation snowballing.
- I did not search for defect or manufacturing work.
- Most of the 34 papers (23) are abstract-only, so their claims are limited to what the abstracts say.
